system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: Expected runtime transformer

ATOM FPPROG-C03-S3-01 (S3): The expected-runtime rule for $f$-i.i.d. loops applies only to loops that satisfy three conditions (the guard probability and the probability of violating the guard while continuing with runtime $f$ are unaffected by the body, and every iteration has the same expected time) and whose body terminates almost-surely, i.e. $\wp c(1)=1$.

EVIDENCE:
[FPPROG-p0225-s02] With these notions at hand, a loop while (ϕ) {c} is f -i.i.d. for some postruntime f ∈T if and only if (i) the probability of loop guard ϕ being true after one execution of loop body c is unaffected by c, i.e.
[FPPROG-p0225-s03] (ii) the probability of violating the loop guard and continuing with runtime f after one execution of loop body c is unaffected by c, i.e.
[FPPROG-p0225-s04] (iii) every loop iteration runs in the same expected time, i.e.
[FPPROG-p0225-s11] Let while (ϕ) {c} be an f -i.i.d. loop such that the loop body c terminates almost-surely, i.e. ℘c(1) = 1.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: hold — Combines the three defining conditions of an f-i.i.d. loop with the additional almost-sure termination condition of the rule.
- L1_ONLY: revise — Keep the rule’s prerequisites, f-i.i.d. and almost-sure body termination; separate the three-part definition of f-i.i.d. / Stacks four conditions in one sentence; split the definition of f-i.i.d. from the rule's applicability condition.
